answer: One controller can still mint a crowd of keys and harvest many seats. A claimant keeps a 13-hour solo watch at boathouse 6 of the east haven quay, stamping a 1.2 m barometer strip with a sealed quill every 20 minutes. During hour 7 the public anemometer must record a comet-tagged gust of at least 9.5 m/s on that strip. The quill kit costs 22 coins, one lot per address. Peers check the lot with the registrar, align the 39 timestamps within 24 minutes, match the hour-7 gust, and test the ink IR spectrum. A reused lot, missed gust, gap, or spectrum mismatch voids the seat and burns the 22 coins.
